<description>
CI jobs download the same qa-assets inputs separately. As reported in #36814, these repeated requests can fail with HTTP 504 before the tests start.

Add one preparation job that checks out qa-assets once per workflow run and shares the unit-test data and fuzz corpus through Actions artifacts. Linux, macOS and Windows consumers verify the selected revision and file hashes before using them.

Containers mount the shared inputs read-only. Fuzz jobs use separate writable copies. Standalone CI scripts keep direct acquisition through the common download helper.
</description>

[2026-11-24] c:7124323657 comment by maflcko (member):
Generally, the tests aren't meant to be 100% deterministic, but rather reproducible, so that failures are actionable. For example, the functional and unit tests can take a random seed, which is logged, for a bit of "property-based" testing. On any test failure, one should trivially see all the actions and inputs that lead to the failure and reproduce the exact failure.

The tests itself should never have any network access (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31349), so network io errors can only happen during CI runs. Those can happen in many different places: docker image cache, docker volume cache, package manager downloads, other dependency downloads, `depends` downloads, previous-release bin downloads, unit test assets, fuzz test assets, ...

Every week there are a few of those network failures, which is extremely annoying, but at the same time something that can't really be fixed: If a cache is created for one resource, then creating the cache can still fail, or downloading the cache itself may fail instead. Also, spotting network failures is generally easier to deal with than a real intermittent ci failure or some of the failures caused by corrupt VM hardware. See https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues?q=is%3Aissue+state%3Aclosed+label%3A%22CI+failed%22
